matrix_role: tests for utility shutoff, medical baseline, extreme heat / cold, outage, PSPS, LIHEAP, emPOWER, cooling, backup-power, and reconnection continuity

CU-01.fail_or_repair: Do not merge outage and nonpayment logic; build an event-type ladder before assigning duty, remedy, or metric.
CU-01.label: Account and event-state split
CU-01.question: Can the packet separate final notice, nonpayment shutoff, reconnection, storm outage, PSPS / de-energization, fuel delivery, arrears, deposit, and payment-plan states before calling service continuous?

CU-02.fail_or_repair: Treat medical flags as stale until equipment, renewal, contact, and backup-power requirements are visible.
CU-02.label: Medical baseline and device inventory
CU-02.question: Does the record identify medical-baseline / serious-illness state, electricity-dependent equipment, medication refrigeration, battery duration, caregiver / representative contact, and renewal clock?

CU-03.fail_or_repair: Do not count assistance as continuity until the utility or vendor record shows the disconnection clock changed.
CU-03.label: Energy-assistance and arrears posting
CU-03.question: Can assistance eligibility, award, vendor posting, shutoff hold, reconnection fee, residual debt, and next bill be traced at account level?

CU-04.fail_or_repair: Do not use ordinary billing or restoration queues when hazard duration exceeds the household life-safety clock.
CU-04.label: Climate hazard and life-safety clock
CU-04.question: Does the packet set a safe-time clock for heat, cold, smoke, storm, battery duration, medication cold chain, elevator / mobility access, and communications?

CU-05.fail_or_repair: A single mailed, emailed, or IVR notice is not enough for medical-baseline or climate-hazard continuity.
CU-05.label: Notice, contact cascade, and representative route
CU-05.question: Does the record show accessible notice and live contact attempts to customer, authorized representative, caregiver, clinician, utility, emergency manager, and community route?

CU-06.fail_or_repair: Do not cite a cooling center, shelter, or preparedness page as safety without transport and compatibility evidence.
CU-06.label: Backup power, cooling, warming, and relocation logistics
CU-06.question: Is there evidence of usable battery / generator / charging support, cooling or warming access, transport, caregiver accommodation, and device-compatible relocation?

CU-07.fail_or_repair: Do not treat medical-baseline enrollment or PSPS notice as energization or life-safety support.
CU-07.label: PSPS and wildfire de-energization boundaries
CU-07.question: Can PSPS authority, affected circuit / territory, medical-baseline notice, actual de-energization, restoration, and vulnerable-customer support be separated?

CU-08.fail_or_repair: Do not close the case at restoration if treatment, debt, or equipment damage remains unresolved.
CU-08.label: Reconnection, restoration, and treatment repair tail
CU-08.question: Does the packet track service restoration, reconnection fees, repeated shutoff risk, food / medication spoilage, equipment damage, missed treatment, and complaint / appeal outcomes?

CU-09.fail_or_repair: Aggregate disconnection counts cannot prove equity or safety without medical, assistance, territory, and climate-event denominators.
CU-09.label: Public metrics and subgroup denominators
CU-09.question: Do public reports separate final notices, shutoffs, reconnections, medical-baseline accounts, assistance posting lag, climate-event disconnections, service territories, and vulnerability denominators?

CU-10.fail_or_repair: Do not count referral as repair until the receiving program has an owner, deadline, and outcome receipt.
CU-10.label: Cross-program handoff and emergency-management route
CU-10.question: Can utility, LIHEAP / energy office, public health, emergency management, disability services, weatherization / repair, and health-system handoffs be traced to an accountable owner?
